# Stack Review Checklist

Use this checklist when reviewing code changes in the git codebase.

---

## C Code Quality

- [ ] No memory leaks — every `xmalloc` / `strbuf_init` has a matching `free` / `strbuf_release`
- [ ] No use of `sprintf` / `strcpy` / `strcat` — use `strbuf_*` or `xsnprintf` APIs
- [ ] Error returns checked — all syscall and I/O return values are tested
- [ ] Object lookups use `repo_find_unique_abbrev` / `parse_object` correctly; NULL checked
- [ ] `struct object_id` passed by pointer, not by value (large struct)
- [ ] `struct strbuf` released before function exit in all code paths

## Build Hygiene

- [ ] `make` completes without warnings (`DEVELOPER=1`)
- [ ] `make check` passes (clang-format / whitespace checks)
- [ ] No new `-Wimplicit-function-declaration` warnings
- [ ] Portability: no POSIX-non-conforming constructs without `compat/` shim

## Style (`.clang-format`)

- [ ] Tabs for indentation, 8-space tab stops
- [ ] Lines ≤ 80 characters where possible
- [ ] Function definitions: return type on its own line (K&R style) [?]
- [ ] `{` brace on same line as control statement
- [ ] No trailing whitespace

## Testing

- [ ] New command or behaviour has a corresponding test script in `t/`
- [ ] Test uses `test_expect_success` / `test_expect_failure` helpers
- [ ] Test is idempotent and cleans up its `trash` directory
- [ ] Unit-testable logic added to `t/unit-tests/` where appropriate
- [ ] `make test` passes locally

## Security

- [ ] User-supplied paths sanitised before shell expansion
- [ ] No `system()` / `popen()` with unsanitised input — use `start_command` API
- [ ] Credential data never logged or written to world-readable files
- [ ] Protocol URL parsing uses `url.c` helpers, not ad-hoc `strchr`

## Object / ODB Access

- [ ] Object reads go through `repo_read_object_file` or `parse_object` (caches correctly)
- [ ] Writes go through `hash_object_file` + `write_object_file` (ensures atomicity)
- [ ] SHA-256 compatibility: code uses `the_hash_algo` indirection, not hardcoded `sha1`
- [ ] Packfile access uses `use_pack` / `unuse_pack` pair correctly

## Ref Operations

- [ ] Ref updates use `ref_transaction_*` API (not direct file writes)
- [ ] Symbolic refs resolved via `resolve_ref_unsafe` before object lookup
- [ ] Ref name validated with `check_refname_format` before creation

## Transport / Network

- [ ] HTTP errors handled (non-200 status codes, curl error codes)
- [ ] Proxy and credential config respected (`http.proxy`, `credential.helper`)
- [ ] Side-band multiplexing used for progress output on smart HTTP/SSH

## Documentation

- [ ] New user-facing option documented in `Documentation/git-<cmd>.txt`
- [ ] `git help <cmd>` renders without AsciiDoc errors [?]
- [ ] Commit message follows 50/72 rule and references related issue/list thread
